## Functions

### `async createRealmLocalOperatorSnapshotSource(options)`

Read one coherent local selection/policy cut for a captured Kernel operator. Options are exactly { operatorContext, selectionStorageView, policyStorageView }. The returned source exposes only readSnapshot({ signal }); it cannot write, select a Realm, allocate a lifecycle, subscribe, or activate a provider. The cut is selection S1 -> selected policy P1 -> exact S1 reassertion. Under the protected sources' trusted/cooperative writer premise, monotonic selection epoch plus exact storage SHA excludes A-B-A and establishes a cut at P1. A policy missing at P1 still requires the final selection check. A missing or cleared initial selection returns no policy and performs no policy I/O. This is point-in-time evidence, not a lease or a promise that the state stays current after return. No lifecycleGeneration or operatorPartitionId is inferred. B4A/B4F still need genuine lifecycle binding and invalidation. These sources require trusted Kernel construction; public classes/view brands do not prove authenticated acquisition, and no shared-origin native OPFS isolation is added.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
